title: Exposure gates priority slate and testing hypotheses (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sketch for a prioritized slate of exposure gates, a lightweight hypothesis template, and operational decision rules to use for cross-functional canaries and A/B tests. It is intended to be pragmatic: fit on a single page for a feature kickoff and expand with scenario-specific numbers.

Audience:
- Product and PMs running feature experiments
- Engineering (serving/runtime teams) responsible for traffic slices and safety hooks
- SRE/Oncall for monitoring and rollback coordination
- Solutions/SE for customer-sensitive launches

Scope:
- Applies to progressive exposure of model-backed features (LLM generation, reranking, embeddings in production) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Focused on gating signals (observability + quality), not on experiment analysis methods (A/A checks, p-values).

Definitions / quick glossary:
- Exposure Gate: a checkpoint where one or more metrics must be within bounds for expansion to continue.
- Slice: a traffic partition (cohort) defined by user attributes, geo, plan_level, or percent of total traffic.
- Commitment Signal: metric(s) that assert we are ready to expand (e.g., latency p95 < target, error rate < threshold, quality regression < delta).
- Safety Trigger: thresholds that immediately pause or rollback exposure and notify oncall.

Hypothesis template (one-liner + quick checks):
- Hypothesis: "If we route cohort X to model variant B, average completion speed improves by >15% without degrading user satisfaction or increasing error rate."
- Primary metric (commitment): p95 latency for text-generation < 450ms and success-rate > 99.7%
- Secondary metrics (watch): token-cost per request, downstream conversion lift, qualitative failure rate from sampled logs
- Acceptance window: no statistically significant regression on secondary metrics across 48h at 5k requests
- Risk notes: increased hallucination risk at longer contexts; requires manual spot review of 100 transcripts after 24h

Priority slate for gates (ranked):
1) Platform health gate (always first):
   - Node GPU OOMs = 0; queue length per shard < 5; autoscaler errors = 0
   - SLO: cluster CPU < 80% and GPU utilization not causing throttling for 95% of time
2) Latency / perf gate:
   - p50, p95, p99 observed and expected under slice load; p95 must be <= target_p95 * 1.1
   - Spike rule: if p99 increases > 2x baseline, mark critical and pause expansion
3) Availability / error gate:
   - 5xx rate < 0.1% (or threshold tied to customer SLA)
   - Request timeouts < 0.05% per slice
4) Quality / safety gate:
   - Manual review signal: sample-failure-rate (human-labeled) < X% (feature-specific)
   - Automated classifier alerts (toxic/harmful outputs) below configured rate
5) Cost signal (soft gate):
   - Per-request token cost delta within budget band (e.g., < +20% unit cost); if breached, require PM signoff
6) Business impact gate (post-activation watch):
   - Conversion/engagement delta within acceptable drift band or positive in pilot cohorts

Gating thresholds: conventions and examples
- Conservative defaults (for new models/features):
  - Latency p95: <= 450ms
  - Error rate (server 5xx): <= 0.1%
  - Quality regression (human score): delta <= 2 percentage points vs baseline
- Iteration defaults (for low-risk changes): relax latency to 600ms, error <= 0.5%
- Always specify absolute numbers for the experiment; these are starting heuristics only

Cohort selection and slice priorities
- Priority slices to seed: internal staff alpha (0.5%), power users/enterprise customers (1–5%), regionally constrained geo (5%), global holdout (remaining)
- Rules: do not mix enterprise+public slices in the same initial cohort; start with low blast radius groups (internal -> alpha customers -> broader)

Instrumentation checklist (quick):
- Tracing hooks instrumented and tied to feature flag ID (ffid)
- Token-level cost and time breakdown for each request
- Sampling pipeline for outputs to be human-labeled (min 100/day for early wave)
- Alerts wired to experiment channel and oncall rota
- Canary slices configured as immutable once live for experiment duration (no underlying routing changes)

Automated vs manual gates
- Automated gates (immediate): platform health, latency, error rate. These should trigger automated pause/rollback and open incident channel.
- Manual gates (human decision): quality regressions from sampled reviews, ambiguous classifier flags, cost overruns where business tradeoff is needed.
- Document which team owns the manual decision (PM + Eng + Safety as needed) and expected SLA for decision (typically 1–2 hours).

Rollback / rollforward decision matrix (quick):
- If automated safety trigger fires: immediate pause + rollback to last stable variant; oncall paged; open incident with "experiment" tag.
- If manual safety concern (human review) shows low-severity but high-frequency failures: hold expansion; require hotfix or model rollback within 24h.
- If cost increase with no quality improvement: pause and consult finance/PM for mitigations (quantization, batching, routing to cheaper region).

Escalation ladder and comms
- Level 1 (owner): PM and eng owner; update experiment doc and Slack channel; sample logs; attempt immediate mitigation (throttle, routing)
- Level 2 (oncall): SRE; assess infra causes; if platform incident, follow SRE incident runbook
- Level 3 (ops + exec oncall): if customer-facing SLA impact or extended outage (>30m) escalate to director oncall and CS lead
- Comms: use experiment channel, incident runbook page, and send a status update to #prod-incidents with subject prefix [EXPERIMENT]

Sample scenario (fast-fail example):
- Feature: new reranker model variant B for search
- Start: 1% internal staff -> monitor 6h -> expand to 5% power users if gates pass
- Observed: p95 jumps from 200ms to 900ms at 2% -> automated latency p95 spike rule triggers -> traffic immediately shifted back to variant A and oncall paged -> PM + Eng decision to rollback; no manual approvals needed

Sample scenario (manual review example):
- Feature: assistant suggestion rewrites
- Start: 0.5% internal -> sample 200 outputs; 8 flagged by internal reviewers for hallucination-type errors (4%)
- Manual gate threshold = 2% -> stop expansion, schedule triage with applied-ml + PM, assign remediation (prompt adjustment + small model change)

Data and analysis guidance (brief):
- Use pre-registered hypothesis fields in the kickoff doc (primary/secondary metrics, slices, stop criteria)
- Run A/A checks for at least 24h for platform variance baseline when changing infra or routing logic
- Keep experiment runtime windows and minima (e.g., min 5k successful requests per slice per day) to avoid noisy signals

Open questions / known gaps (for this WIP):
- Granularity for cost gating per-customer for Dedicated tenants (should thresholds be tenant-specific?)
- How to standardize human-review taxonomy across product areas (label schema suggestion needed)
- Integration with rollout UI: how to show auto-gate status and allow owner approvals without granting broad console privileges

Immediate next steps and owners:
- Align on default conservative thresholds (Maya)
- Draft label taxonomy for sampled outputs (Leila + Jonah)
- Hook automated pause action into feature-flag system (ENG: Evan)
- Mock a UI tile that surfaces gate status + one-click rollback (Design + ENG)

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add quick simulation tool to estimate p95 impact when moving from A -> B given qps distribution (link to INF-4321)
- Capture examples of noisy metrics (e.g., weekend vs weekday) and recommended minimum observation windows

References and useful links:
- Rollout templates (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/rollout-templates
- Infra ticket for automated pause action: INF-4321
- PR prototype for gate-runbook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts/pull/98

End of working draft. Add comments inline, mark sections you want trimmed to a one-pager for PM kickoff.
